- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The establishment of the Historical Centre of Rome was initiated by the Italian government in 1980, which includes most of the city's ancient landmarks.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Italian government has initiated and supported several restoration projects on ancient landmarks such as the Colosseum, the Roman Forum, and the Pantheon.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Italian government has issued several protection laws, notably the 1939 Law on Protection of Historic Monuments and Sites, to protect historical landmarks from decay and destruction.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Italy has collaborated with international organizations such as UNESCO to protect and preserve its historical landmarks, with the Historic Centre of Rome being declared a World Heritage Site in 1980.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Several private organizations and individuals have contributed to the preservation of historical landmarks by donating funds to initiate restoration projects.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The number of tourists visiting some of Rome's popular landmarks has been limited to preserve them.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] New historical landmarks and artifacts are constantly being discovered in Rome.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In 2018, archaeologists discovered an intact 2,000-year-old sarcophagus containing the remains of a middle-aged woman in the city center.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In January 2021, Italian authorities announced the discovery of a rare Roman sarcophagus from a luxury villa on the outskirts of the city.
